papers.title: Generic structure and rhetorical moves in English-language empirical law research articles: Sites of interdisciplinary and interdiscursive cross-over
papers.scope: Empirical socio-legal research articles for scholarly readership, 2010–2012, three selected English-language journals; not theoretical legal essays, court decisions, or policy proposals.
papers.sample_and_design: 90 randomly selected Article-category papers, 30 per journal and 10 per journal-year; 1,079,527 tokens excluding footnotes and references. Manual functional-semantic analysis of headings, clause/sentence moves and frequencies. Selection restricts journal and article type (PDF p. 3 Tables 1–2, p. 4).
papers.outcomes: Section heading categories, rhetorical macro-organization, move and step frequencies, and selected lexical realizations; no reader experiment or writing-quality causal outcome.

Abstract: Setting the background for the study and its importance
Mentioning gaps addressed by the study
Stating the purpose, question, hypothesis of study
Stating the findings (qualitative or quantitative) or argument
Results: Restating data collection and analysis procedure

9: Announcing present research descriptively and/or purposively
12: Defining and developing methods, theories, concepts, issues, phenomena
Presenting the value of the study
15: Describing measures of variability for significant difference

findings.claim: Background review present in 79, absent in 11.
findings.interpretation_limit: Presence does not mandate a separate section; heading genres vary.

findings.claim: 75 independent Conclusion sections, and seven Discussion/Conclusion or Discussion/Implications blends; 82 total independent plus blended conclusions.
findings.interpretation_limit: Section-level pattern, not a paragraph function quota.

findings.claim: 12 blended-section occurrences: 1 Methods/Results, 4 Results/Discussion and 7 Discussion/Conclusion.
findings.denominator: 90 articles; 12 occurrences, not verified as 12 distinct documents
findings.interpretation_limit: Blending may coexist with separate analytical units.

findings.claim: 25 moves, with 6/3/3/3/3/4/3 per Abstract/Introduction/Background Review/Method/Results/Discussion/Conclusion; recursively patterned in every section and occasionally inverted.
findings.denominator: 90 selected articles; the claim every section is author statement

findings.claim: Abstract moves purpose, methodology, findings, conclusion each 100%; background 44%, gap 28%.
findings.interpretation_limit: Step percentages are ambiguous in denominator: avoid converting to counts.

findings.claim: Author reports 100% inter-rater agreement with one other applied-linguistics author.
findings.denominator: Coding sample size, independent/consensus protocol and metric not specified
findings.interpretation_limit: Do not compare directly to our exact-set agreement.

limitations: Table 3 says 33 unlabelled introductions but prints 27%; 33/90 is 36.7%. Its Results heading subtotals 65+10+15=90 despite underlying journal rows summing to more than 90; do not silently repair.
Step percentages generally sum to 100 within a move but denominator is not clearly stated; do not convert them into article prevalence.
Authors use obligatory for 100% observed corpus moves; sample and coding not a universal requirement.
Supplementary list of article identities mentioned PDF p.3 footnote; annotated corpus release not verified.
data_or_code_leads: PDF p.3 footnote says full sampled article list is in supplementary materials; actual files and terms unverified.
extraction_issues: Table 3 contains arithmetic inconsistencies as printed; Table 5 multiline rows retain blank 16A frequency.

papers.title: In search of commonalities: Some linguistic and rhetorical features of business reports as a genre
papers.study_kind: primarily qualitative descriptive genre corpus study
papers.scope: Authentic internal and external business reports, mainly Hong Kong with Singapore, Malaysia and UK sources, prepared for organizational clients, management, stakeholders or public; not a sample of decision memos per se.
papers.sample_and_design: 22 nonrandom convenience samples submitted by organizations; 12 external and 10 internal, 7 review, 6 problem-solving, 5 market and 4 feasibility reports. Management authors and some collective authorship; writers interviewed where possible, exact interview count not given (PDF pp. 4–6).
papers.outcomes: Observed macro organization, recommendations, rhetorical patterns and lexico-grammar; not independent measurement of decision outcomes or reader comprehension.

macro_options: topical sections containing findings and interpretations/conclusions

papers.step_inventory: Finding, interpretation and recommendation can occur in varying order and recur by topic; Toulmin roles are analytical relations, not mandatory paragraph sequence (PDF pp. 10, 14).

findings.claim: 19 reports contain clearly stated recommendations, and seven have clear recommendation headings; elsewhere paper says only two reports lack explicit recommendations.
findings.interpretation_limit: 19+2 does not account for all 22 under apparently similar wording; unresolved rather than silently reconciled.

findings.claim: Four conclusion sections, all summaries of recommendations; one report used the described conventional heading pattern.
findings.interpretation_limit: Predominantly qualitative, small heterogeneous convenience sample.
Historical descriptive range only, not a target or minimum/maximum.

findings.claim: One full-length feasibility report has a separate clearly labelled methods section; methods otherwise often brief or absent.
findings.interpretation_limit: Paper says no examples of extensive appendical methods in corpus; brief reporting is not evidence that omitting methods is safe.

findings.claim: The suggested data/interpretation/recommendation sequence can vary; warrants may be implicit or explicit.
findings.denominator: Qualitative across corpus; no exact count for the cycle
findings.interpretation_limit: Do not force three moves or infer implicit support without contextual judgment.

limitations: Organizations supplied examples, not random or representative; mostly Hong Kong and medium/large firms. Paper stresses its qualitative size limitation and seeks quantitative replication (pp. 5, 22–23).
19/22 vs only two without explicit recommendation wording is unresolved.
No coder agreement method or downloadable coded dataset identified in full text; example business figures anonymized.
The author claims an inherent implicit recommendation even for sales reports; inference, not a directly observed reader action.
data_or_code_leads: No open coded data or codebook release identified in paper; quotations contain confidential anonymization.
extraction_issues: Observed numbers 19 with clearly stated recommendations and two without explicit recommendations are textually inconsistent; preserve as reported.

papers.title: A move/step model for methods sections: Demonstrating Rigour and Credibility
papers.study_kind: multidisciplinary descriptive corpus and expert-consultation study
papers.scope: Methods sections of IMRD experimental research articles; excludes disciplines whose scholarship differs substantially, such as mathematics, statistics, architecture and history (PDF p. 4).
papers.sample_and_design: 900 texts in 30 disciplines, 30 selected articles per discipline from 3–5 reputable journals; 150 exemplary sections seeded coding; expert-selected recent studies and one consultant per discipline limit representativeness; 1,423,131 words. Human annotations with sentence/phrase units and secondary overlapping functions (PDF pp. 3–6).
papers.outcomes: Functional-semantic move/step inventories and annotated unit frequency, sequences, consultant perceived occurrence, discipline clustering. No direct test of improved writing outcomes.
papers.step_inventory: Six, seven and three steps, respectively; see move_inventory counts and names. Numbering is not a prescribed order. Table 3 labels counts as sentences, while surrounding text calls overall counts functional units; sentence/phrase overlaps preclude treating these as independently observed document prevalence (PDF pp. 6, 8, 10, 12).

findings.claim: Three annotators: ICC .86 for moves and .80 for steps, using a two-way mixed-effects model, calculated throughout.
findings.denominator: three annotators; number and sampling of doubly/triply coded units unspecified
findings.interpretation_limit: ICC is not our paragraph exact-set agreement; no metric equivalence or accuracy claim.

findings.claim: 94,925 annotated functional units: 21,397 Move 1 (22%), 67,337 Move 2 (71%), 6,191 Move 3 (7%).
findings.interpretation_limit: Paper describes Move 1 as optional based on distribution but also says all 900 texts contain it; unit share is not document prevalence.

findings.claim: All 16 steps observed overall; Table 3 lists within-move sentence counts including Move 2 tools 30,693/67,337 = 45.6%.
findings.denominator: move-specific counts; table labels them sentences and allows overlapping functional tags
findings.interpretation_limit: No claim that 45.6% of documents have this step or should allocate that much space.

findings.claim: All seven Move 2 steps occur in each of 30 disciplines at aggregate level; Move 3 absent from some individual texts.
findings.interpretation_limit: Discipline-level presence does not imply occurrence in each paper.

findings.claim: Reporting incrementals identified in all 30 disciplines; experts report it as rare 40% or lacking 8%.
findings.denominator: 30 disciplines for corpus; consultant response denominator not explicitly clear from extracted text
findings.interpretation_limit: Expert judgments and corpus measurements have different units; interpret contrast, not exact contradiction.

findings.claim: Step transition likelihoods computed on the larger related IMRD corpus; reported zero transitions are sample/model observations.
findings.denominator: Related larger corpus includes Methods sample, so not independent replication
findings.interpretation_limit: Do not forbid zero-probability transitions in new writing.

limitations: One faculty consultant per discipline, purposively selected 30 studies per field, and explicitly excluded non-IMRD disciplinary traditions; no representative prevalence claim.
Paper does not perform full lexico-grammatical realization analysis (PDF p.16).
Unit share vs document presence conflated in author’s optionality label; do not adopt.
One source paragraph misnames Move 2 Step 7 as rationalizing, whereas inventory and definition show Step 6 rationalizing and Step 7 reporting incrementals (PDF pp.9,15).
Original study imposes primary label and secondary label; this project does not require a primary function.
data_or_code_leads: Authors report annotated corpus used through Callisto or other platforms and a move/step functional concordancer (PDF pp.15–16); release URL, data rights, model and corpus files remain unverified.
extraction_issues: Table 3 labels step frequencies sentences; paper elsewhere calls totals functional segments. Report denominator as printed and preserve overlap.

conclusions: Section purpose and nested move/step structure are useful candidates but are not equivalent to the twelve local passage functions or relation graphs.
Allow repeated, embedded, non-linear and blended contributions; empirical presence, annotated unit share and author template requirements are distinct.
A blank prompt can ask for author ideas and missing decision logic; it must not insert borrowed findings, prefabricated claims or a default sequence.
Our 21/36 versus 18/36 exact-set result is a small model-coder pilot; none of these papers tests improvement on the same units, nor supplies semantic gold or full function-length profiles.

twelve_function_comparison.orient: background and contextualizing may orient when preparing a reader, not just because located first
twelve_function_comparison.define: Tessuto defining concepts can define if it establishes meaning; mere reference is insufficient
twelve_function_comparison.report: Methods descriptions, facts and empirical findings often report with source/status preserved
twelve_function_comparison.assert: Recommendation or hypothesis can assert when writer advances it; reported opposing claims are not author endorsement
twelve_function_comparison.support: Rationale or evidence can support only with a recoverable target and reasoning link
twelve_function_comparison.explain: A described methodology can explain a dependency but not every list of actions establishes one
twelve_function_comparison.illustrate: Concrete examples can illustrate; evidence and illustration can coexist without equivalence
twelve_function_comparison.compare: Evaluations compare only if alternatives and dimension are recoverable
twelve_function_comparison.interpret: Findings commentary or implication can interpret if it adds an inference, not faithful recap
twelve_function_comparison.qualify: Limitation can qualify a specific claim when its affected scope is identifiable
twelve_function_comparison.instruct: Reader-directed action can instruct; completed research methods report, not instruct by default
twelve_function_comparison.narrate: Temporal event development may narrate; research procedure order alone does not establish a narrative

proposed_rule_changes.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/references/structure-and-purpose.md: For a decision or operational explanation, make the choice, reasons and consequences recoverable.
proposed_rule_changes.trigger: Actual decision work with an audience and a live choice
proposed_rule_changes.change: Offer optional blank prompts for decision, observations, decision criteria/warrant, interpretation, alternatives and constraints. Ask only for relevant information; author chooses sequence and completeness.
proposed_rule_changes.benefit: Makes the recommendation’s connection to evidence reviewable.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: A status-only sales report may legitimately have no explicit recommendation; an implicit one must not be invented.

proposed_rule_changes.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/accepted-foundations.md: Family → Form → Section; section need not have a heading; preserve variation.
proposed_rule_changes.trigger: Author requests outline for an empirical article or comparable evidence-backed report
proposed_rule_changes.change: Show section jobs and optional alternative arrangements, with blends and recursion allowed; classify sections from purpose plus context rather than heading.
proposed_rule_changes.benefit: Offers reusable options without flattening discipline-specific practices.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: A section called Results can include interpretations and an unheaded Introduction can orient.

proposed_rule_changes.trigger: Draft contains recommendation and potential reasons
proposed_rule_changes.change: Independently note recommendation, evidence, warrant, attribution and any relation target; prompt for a missing link only when contextual review finds one needed.
proposed_rule_changes.benefit: Supports examination of the inference instead of treating one label as another.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: A bare citation, juxtaposition or claim that a warrant is implicit does not demonstrate actual support.

proposed_rule_changes.existing_rule: experiments/rule-calibration-2026-11-16/report.md: no demonstrated agreement improvement; evidence anchors are not full realization spans.
proposed_rule_changes.trigger: Imported sentence or phrase roles mapped to paragraph functions
proposed_rule_changes.change: Keep original source labels and overlapping spans, separate evidence anchors and complete realization spans, preserve uncertain and multiple readings, and run a fresh independent boundary study.
proposed_rule_changes.benefit: Makes disagreements inspectable and prevents unit conversion from manufacturing certainty.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: Cotos ICC on a different unit and scheme does not establish improved exact-set agreement on our 36 paragraphs.

proposed_rule_changes.existing_rule: skills/edit-with-purpose/SKILL.md: preserve effective wording and apply smallest targeted change.
proposed_rule_changes.trigger: Author asks for Methods section planning or structural review
proposed_rule_changes.change: Offer context/design; study/data, tools and procedures; data preparation/analysis and reasons as optional questions, not required sections or draft language.
proposed_rule_changes.benefit: Prompts recoverable reporting and design rationale in suitable empirical studies.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: A theoretical paper, a procedure, or a business report can legitimately lack the full experimental Methods structure.

github_reuse.README: README source roles such as What and Why are section-level possibilities, not automatically paragraph roles; sampled roles differ in purpose from research articles and business reports.
github_reuse.DITA: Task section components can represent reader-directed prerequisites/actions/results; completed experimental procedures are report, not reader instruction.
github_reuse.BAWE: Educational genre families and stages are separate from professional business reports and discipline-specific research articles; preserve audience and provenance.
github_reuse.GUM: Discourse relations can link source and target, distinct from moves/steps; implicit warrants remain open semantic questions, not inferred edges.
github_reuse.MuLMS: Scientific annotated functions and overlapping spans invite comparison, but scientific labeling does not provide gold for local twelve functions.
github_reuse.shared: Adapters can check offsets, vocabulary, source and target IDs; judgments of adequacy, inference, meaning, style and author intent require contextual human review.

open_questions: What are each paper’s exact article-level move denominators, step coding protocol and available data rights?
Can independently coded complete realization spans and nonempty relation targets achieve useful agreement on our fresh target forms?
Do author-selected blank template prompts improve reader outcomes and author control compared with current planning without increasing burden?
What public or cleared contemporary professional proposals and decision memos fill the scope gap?
